LIGHT FOR THE LIONS

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Few expected it – the groundbreaking recommendations by Minister Barbara Creecy to finally put an end to captive bred lion hunting, lion bone trading and its derivatives.

Summary:
She has instructed her Department to put processes in place to halt the sale of captive lion derivatives (including the appropriate disposal of existing lion bone stockpiles and lion bone from euthanised lions); the hunting of captive bred lions; tourist interactions with captive lions etc.

It’s a battle hard won and the 582 page report which is extremely comprehensive, doesn’t tell the story of the diverse group of scientists, film – makers, a British lord, and other big cat warriors, who just kept hammering down the barricades for decades even though years went by when their fight seemed hopeless, as lion farms proliferated across the Free State, North West, Eastern Cape and Limpopo. Some had almost given up – Karen Trendler was on the panel and faced such hostility, that she resigned.


Further information:
In a February Zoom meeting organised by Blood Lions, Dr Paul Funston, Panthera’s Southern African director almost broke down, as he recollected the instances of cruelty he had seen. His sentiments were shared by none other than Lord Ashcroft who recounted how he had used his British military contacts and a considerable sum of his own money to expose the appalling cruelty that masqueraded as hunting on South African Lion farms.

“Opposing this brutal industry has been a long journey. Our ultimate objective has always been to end the captive lion breeding industry, and after so many setbacks, we sense an important change in attitude. We applaud the Minister, her department and the HLP. Going forward, we hope to be of assistance to them in closing down the industry", says Ian Michler, Director of Blood Lions.

But it’s not going to be an easy process there are an estimated 8000 – 12 000 lions on these farms with no conservation value. They cannot be reintroduced into the wild and in all probability will have to be humanely euthanised.

Expect a fight, possibly even a legal battle from the lion breeders.

Carte Blanche speaks to these wildlife warriors who never gave up hope, including Lord Ashcroft; to the minister who did the right thing; and the hunters from PHASA. For once a dark story has an ending that brings a ray of hope.

Press Release:


Drawing a Lion in the Sand

Carte Blanche first broadcast the Cooke Report exposé on canned lion hunting in 1997. Two decades later, the captive lion industry has expanded in scope and brutality – cubs are removed from their mothers, hand-reared, petted, then bred for the bullet or their bones. But these practices began to damage Brand SA and, by 2019, the new minister of Environment, Forestry and Fisheries, Barbara Creecy appointed a high-level panel to advise her on the next steps for this industry. Last Sunday, she released her recommendations in an almost 600-page report. The findings signal a seismic shift away from captive breeding and hunting toward a new era for wildlife conservation in South Africa. The news is good for our struggling tourism sector and quickly went global. But will the multi-million rand hunting industry take these changes lying down?

Producer: Joy Summers | Presenter: Masa Kekana

Script:


FINAL SCRIPT –LIONS IN THE SAND/ LIGHT FOR THE LIONS
TX SUNDAY 9th MAY 2021

Commentary One
More than two decades ago, Carte Blanche was the first South African programme to expose our Canned lion hunting industry

LION SHOT

Commentary Two
Around the same time, photojournalist Ian Michler was starting his OWN investigation. It was a hard and lonely journey

Ian Michler
A lot of people just didn’t believe the stories. When I would write articles they would say ya ok that’s terrible but with a lack of a powerful visual narrative they found it very difficult to comprehend.

Commentary Three
It was also dangerous trying to gather undercover evidence

Up sound
I give you two minutes two minutes to leave my property ...you are from the greenies

Ian
I was physically attacked on one of the properties and that was always my fear –to be physically trapped on one of those properties with those gates closing

Commentary Four
He wanted to show the world how lion breeders and lodge owners were lying to the public, and how this iconic species, was subjected to unspeakable cruelty

Ian Michler
I cannot express to you enough how brutal this industry is, the commercialization, the commodification, If you have any sense of spirituality that embraces this notion of wilderness and wild, then it cannot be right that a species like lion is brutalized in this manner

Commentary Five
By 2015 he had enough evidence to release Blood Lions, and simultaneously launch a campaign to appeal for an end to this practice

Ian
And then the world started coming on board. We took the story international. We have done presentations in the European parliament twice in Brussels ...Swedish parliament




Commentary Six
But if the world was on board, South Africa wasn’t. Lion breeding farms, cub petting and captive hunting, proliferated across several provinces. But it didn’t stop there, the lions were being bred for their bones and the bullet, and the Department of Environmental affairs made it legal through a permit system

Masa
Did you ever feel despondent?
Ian
Yes of course. Despondency is a companion in these fights. We are dealing with an immensely brutal cruel industry, and people who haven’t been onto these properties will never understand the visual impact of that brutality, so that stays with you, but it was also a driver for me that I carried those visuals with me

Commentary Seven
By 2018, captive lions had increased in number to around eight to 12 thousand. And the issue had split the hunting industry. At the time both SAPA representing breeders, and PHASA representing hunters, defended the practice and Derek Watts confronted PHASA’S Richard York.

Derek
All I am asking you to acknowledge is that captive bred lion hunting is damaging the image of the country as a hunting destination
Richard York
I will not acknowledge that sir because its factually incorrect.

Commentary eight
The hunters who have rejected captive hunting, call themselves Custodians of Professional Hunting and Conservation SA

Paul Stones
It was a practice that we could not justify, it was a practice that was condemned by everybody basically, in the hunting world

Commentary nine
Internationally, brand South Africa was starting to take a knock. Lord Ashcroft, an influential member of the Conservative party, got involved

Lord Michael Ashcroft
Initially I just couldn't believe that what I was being told was true

Commentary ten
He rallied his contacts, and dug deep into his pockets


LORD ASHCROFT
I recruited a team of operatives, including, former members of the special forces who worked on two undercover operations over two years to infiltrate the lion farming industry.

Commentary Eleven
And he still gets emotional when he recalls what he saw

Lord Ashcroft
You know, there are some memories for me that I will never forget, and that is when I chartered a helicopter, put a very good camera on the front and with special forces people piloting, flew over a number of these farms and saw at first hand the pens in which the lions were kept.

Commentary Twelve
His operatives took photographs of the lions stripped for their bones, and he revealed his findings in a documentary and a book called Unfair Game.

Lord Ashcroft
It was highly emotional, it was highly horrific and the way that these people were conning the public in terms of lying to tourists and petting lines of mothers had abandoned. But yet, at the back of a house that was a slaughter house and in two days, one of my investigators found 54 lions having been shot for their bones. Horrific.

Commentary Thirteen
Then a slight shift in fortunes for the lions. The NSPCA won a landmark case against the DEA, forcing the Ministry to consider the welfare of the lions. But it was only in 2019 that the issue was taken seriously, when the new minister Barbara Creecy appointed a high level panel of 25 members to come up with a solution. Chairlady Pam Yako.

PAM
It was time to think big, but at the same time clean up our house
Masa
I get a sense that not only was brand SA considered but also the welfare of the animals was very critical?
Pam
Yes- because if we don’t look after the welfare of the animals and also the benefits for the people, what is brand SA?

Commentary Fourteen
The twenty five panelists were made up of scientists, hunters, activists, traditional leaders and others.

Yako
The minister when she came to address us she said a couple of things, one was that she respected our independence as the panel and she also said interestingly that you are probably the CODESA of this sector. She then said we would like to be advised on these things but- blank cheque. We will see what you come up with.

Commentary fifteen
They were given a year, and did most of their work during lockdown

LINK
As the long covid days drew on last year, the high level panel continued to slog away- often it got tense – but the chair told them just to trust the process

Pam
But we are talking and talking but we are going nowhere and I kept saying to them, I hear you but let’s trust the process

Commentary sixteen
Yako had to keep the peace. It wasn’t always easy

PAM
There are moments personally that I felt, I am so tempted to just give someone a warm klap and I am sure others too.

Commentary seventeen
But she also began to realise something exceptional was taking shape

PAM
someone came in and she said before I start my representation to the panel, I just want us to stop and call on the ancestors to bless us in this moment and this panel in its work. That was a moment when I felt there is something big here

Commentary eighteen
They accepted more than 70 detailed submissions from across the board

Masa
Blood lions also made submissions, what did you ask for?
Ian
Right from the beginning our primary objective was to end the exploitative breeding of these predators and then all the practices that go with that, cub petting, canned hunting, ranch hunting, walking with lions, the lion bone trade everything to do with that

Commentary nineteen
Last Sunday, the 2nd of May, the minister made the recommendations public

Up sound minister
The panel recommends that South Africa does not captive breed lions, keep lions in captivity or use captive lions or their derivatives commercially

Masa
Does the panel represent a massive shift in conservation and tourism
Pam
Yes it does! MINISTER refers to it when she came to talk to us she said this is the new deal for people and nature – just listening to her say that it was heart- warming

MINISTER
I have requested the department to action this accordingly, and ensure the necessary consultation for implementation is conducted

LINK
For the activists and conservationists who have spent years trying to get government to change its stance on the captive lion industry, last Sunday’s announcement came as a surprise

Ian Michler
We had no idea this was going to happen on Sunday. We had been let down so many times in the past. And what has happened is that rather than listen to a minority voice that was made up of a commercial lobby, the minister and the panel have been able to go through scientific fact based submissions and we got that on Sunday! It was a shift in thinking.

Commentary Twenty
But not everyone seems happy. Sapa says some of the report’s recommendations may have far reaching effects on the industry, and it would engage the minister and the High Level Panel to try reach a workable solution. SAPA says it remains committed to the legal, ethical, breeding and keeping of lions in SA. PHASA is studying the document before it will comment. But expect a pushback and possible legal action. The captive lion industry isn’t going to go quietly

THE END 10 10

PROMO ONE
The Captive lion industry has damaged brand South Africa. Now a High level panel appointed by Minister Barbara Creecy has called for an end to this practice

PROMO TWO
Photojournalist Ian Michler has been campaigning against captive lions for more than two decades. Now a high level panel has recommended the industry be phased out

PROMO THREE
For more than two decades Carte Blanche has followed the story of captive bred lions. Now a glimmer of light for these predators, as government moves to stop the industry









Masa
Take us back to Sunday when Minister Creecy made that announcement
Ian
Laughs.. We suspected that we were going to get something more positive than we were expecting a year ago or even six months ago, but no we didn’t expect the minister to go as far as she did – it was almost unbelievable

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Few expected it – the groundbreaking recommendations by Minister Barbara Creecy to finally put an end to captive bred lion hunting, lion bone trading and its derivatives.
metadata.Summary: She has instructed her Department to put processes in place to halt the sale of captive lion derivatives (including the appropriate disposal of existing lion bone stockpiles and lion bone from euthanised lions); the hunting of captive bred lions; tourist interactions with captive lions etc. It’s a battle hard won and the 582 page report which is extremely comprehensive, doesn’t tell the story of the diverse group of scientists, film – makers, a British lord, and other big cat warriors, who just kept hammering down the barricades for decades even though years went by when their fight seemed hopeless, as lion farms proliferated across the Free State, North West, Eastern Cape and Limpopo. Some had almost given up – Karen Trendler was on the panel and faced such hostility, that she resigned.
metadata.Further information: In a February Zoom meeting organised by Blood Lions, Dr Paul Funston, Panthera’s Southern African director almost broke down, as he recollected the instances of cruelty he had seen. His sentiments were shared by none other than Lord Ashcroft who recounted how he had used his British military contacts and a considerable sum of his own money to expose the appalling cruelty that masqueraded as hunting on South African Lion farms. “Opposing this brutal industry has been a long journey. Our ultimate objective has always been to end the captive lion breeding industry, and after so many setbacks, we sense an important change in attitude. We applaud the Minister, her department and the HLP. Going forward, we hope to be of assistance to them in closing down the industry", says Ian Michler, Director of Blood Lions. But it’s not going to be an easy process there are an estimated 8000 – 12 000 lions on these farms with no conservation value. They cannot be reintroduced into the wild and in all probability will have to be humanely euthanised. Expect a fight, possibly even a legal battle from the lion breeders. Carte Blanche speaks to these wildlife warriors who never gave up hope, including Lord Ashcroft; to the minister who did the right thing; and the hunters from PHASA. For once a dark story has an ending that brings a ray of hope.
